question.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1-{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 1 \\ \frac{8}{9{x}^{3}}, & 1<x\le 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{3}].$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the $n$th raw moment of $X$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{n}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{n}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the third raw moment of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{3}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{3}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\cdot (1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{3}\cdot \frac{8}{9{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}-{x}^{5})\,\text{d}x+\frac{8}{9}{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}\,{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{6}\,{x}^{6}){|}_{0}^{1}+\frac{8}{9}\,x\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6}-0)+\frac{8}{9}(2-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}+\frac{8}{9} \\  & =\frac{35}{36}\end{aligned}
$$
